entries.caveat: The analyzer returns 3 decimals (5.901 A mean over 2,012 backbone bonds, 0 violations), so the panel prints one digit more than the function produces.

entries.measured_recipe: pdb_analyzer.compute_pair_satisfaction on the committed PDB: 5,532 P-P pairs within 15 A, 1,723 of them Watson-Crick complements, 814 of those within 12 A -> 814/1723 = 47.2%.
entries.note: docs/REPRODUCTION_RESOURCES.md section 5 attributes this 100.0% to compute_pair_satisfaction. That function returns 47.2% on this structure, so the attribution does not hold. Three different quantities in this codebase are called 'pair rate' and only one of them is structure-inferred: (a) pdb_analyzer.compute_pair_satisfaction, WC-complement filtered, 15 A neighbourhood, 12 A criterion -- 47.2% here; (b) isrnaclong._compute_pair_rate(coords, pairs), a fraction over the PREDICTED pair list with a 12 A criterion -- this is the 100% family, and it is near-tautological when the pair list is read off the structure it scores; (c) isrnaclong._validate_structure's pair_rate, the same but at 15 A. The panel value is consistent with (b)/(c), not with (a). Whether the panel label, the doc, or neither should change is a maintainer decision; this file records the measurement so the choice is made on a number.
